name: ISO 27001
description: Annex A controls from ISO/IEC 27001:2022. Titles identify the control. Descriptions are our own short guidance, not the standard's text. Clauses 4 to 10 are not part of this seed.

requirements.title: Organizational controls
requirements.summary: Controls that sit with the organization rather than a single system.

children.title: Policies for information security
children.summary: Write the security rules down, have management approve them, and tell people where they live.

children.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
children.summary: Name who protects information, who they report to, and what they are accountable for.

children.title: Segregation of duties
children.summary: Split sensitive work so one person cannot both request and approve it.

children.title: Management responsibilities
children.summary: Managers make sure their teams follow the security rules.

children.title: Contact with authorities
children.summary: Know which regulators and law-enforcement contacts you will call, and when.

children.title: Contact with special interest groups
children.summary: Keep a link to security communities that share warnings relevant to you.

children.title: Threat intelligence
children.summary: Collect useful threat information and use it to adjust your defenses.

children.title: Information security in project management
children.summary: Put security checkpoints into projects, not only into day-to-day operations.

children.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
children.summary: Keep a list of the information and systems you rely on, and who owns each one.

children.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
children.summary: Tell people what they may and may not do with company systems and data.

children.title: Return of assets
children.summary: Collect equipment and access when someone stops needing them.

children.title: Classification of information
children.summary: Label information by how sensitive it is so people handle it consistently.

children.title: Labelling of information
children.summary: Mark sensitive information in a way people and systems can recognize.

children.title: Information transfer
children.summary: Protect information when it moves between people, systems, or organizations.

children.title: Access control
children.summary: Give people access only to what their work requires.

children.title: Identity management
children.summary: Give each person a unique identity and keep the lifecycle of that identity under control.

children.title: Authentication information
children.summary: Protect passwords, keys, and other secrets people use to prove who they are.

children.title: Access rights
children.summary: Review and adjust access when jobs change, and remove it when it is no longer needed.

children.title: Information security in supplier relationships
children.summary: Expect suppliers who touch your systems or data to meet your security bar.

children.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
children.summary: Put the security obligations in the contract, not only in a conversation.

children.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
children.summary: Understand security risk in the chain of technology suppliers behind a service.

children.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
children.summary: Recheck supplier services when they change, and on a regular schedule.

children.title: Information security for use of cloud services
children.summary: Decide how cloud services are chosen, configured, and left.

children.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
children.summary: Decide in advance who responds to a security incident and how.

children.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
children.summary: Triage security events so real incidents get a response.

children.title: Response to information security incidents
children.summary: Contain and fix incidents using the plan you prepared.

children.title: Learning from information security incidents
children.summary: Record what an incident taught you and change the system accordingly.

children.title: Collection of evidence
children.summary: When you need evidence, collect it in a way that preserves it.

children.title: Information security during disruption
children.summary: Keep security in place when the business is operating in a degraded mode.

children.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
children.summary: Make sure technology can be recovered in the time the business can tolerate.

children.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
children.summary: Know the legal and contractual security duties that apply and track them.

children.title: Intellectual property rights
children.summary: Use software and content within the rights you actually have.

children.title: Protection of records
children.summary: Keep required records readable and protected for as long as you must.

children.title: Privacy and protection of PII
children.summary: Handle personal information in line with the privacy commitments you make.

children.title: Independent review of information security
children.summary: Have someone independent check the security program on a schedule.

children.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
children.summary: Check that teams actually follow the security rules you published.

children.title: Documented operating procedures
children.summary: Write down how to operate systems so the work does not live in one person's head.

requirements.title: People controls
requirements.summary: Controls that depend on how people are hired, trained, and offboarded.

children.title: Screening
children.summary: Screen people before you trust them with access, at a level that matches the role.

children.title: Terms and conditions of employment
children.summary: Put security responsibilities into the employment terms people agree to.

children.title: Information security awareness, education and training
children.summary: Train people for the security risks in their actual job.

children.title: Disciplinary process
children.summary: Have a fair process for when someone breaks the security rules.

children.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
children.summary: When someone leaves or changes role, end their access and remind them of ongoing duties.

children.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
children.summary: Use confidentiality terms with people who will see sensitive information.

children.title: Remote working
children.summary: Set expectations for working outside the office, including how devices are protected.

children.title: Information security event reporting
children.summary: Make it easy and expected for people to report a security concern.

requirements.title: Physical controls
requirements.summary: Controls for facilities, equipment, and the spaces people work in.

children.title: Physical security perimeters
children.summary: Define the physical boundary around spaces that need protection.

children.title: Physical entry
children.summary: Control and record who enters secure areas.

children.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
children.summary: Lock rooms that hold sensitive work, and don't leave them open by habit.

children.title: Physical security monitoring
children.summary: Watch physical spaces for unauthorized access.

children.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
children.summary: Plan for fire, water, heat, and similar threats to facilities and equipment.

children.title: Working in secure areas
children.summary: Set extra rules for people working inside a secure area.

children.title: Clear desk and clear screen
children.summary: Lock screens and put sensitive papers away when you step away.

children.title: Equipment siting and protection
children.summary: Place equipment so it is harder to steal, view, or damage.

children.title: Security of assets off-premises
children.summary: Protect equipment and data that leave the building.

children.title: Storage media
children.summary: Control storage media through its life, including when it is reused or sent out.

children.title: Supporting utilities
children.summary: Protect power and other utilities the systems depend on.

children.title: Cabling security
children.summary: Protect network and power cables from tampering and accidental damage.

children.title: Equipment maintenance
children.summary: Maintain equipment so it stays reliable and so maintenance staff don't get open-ended access.

children.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
children.summary: Wipe or destroy storage before equipment is reused or thrown away.

requirements.title: Technological controls
requirements.summary: Controls implemented in systems, software, and networks.

children.title: User endpoint devices
children.summary: Protect laptops and other endpoints that people use for work.

children.title: Privileged access rights
children.summary: Limit administrator access and keep it separate from everyday accounts.

children.title: Information access restriction
children.summary: Restrict access to information and system functions to the people who need them.

children.title: Access to source code
children.summary: Limit who can read and change source code.

children.title: Secure authentication
children.summary: Use authentication that resists guessing, replay, and stolen-password reuse.

children.title: Capacity management
children.summary: Watch capacity so systems keep up with demand.

children.title: Protection against malware
children.summary: Protect systems from malware and know what to do when it is found.

children.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
children.summary: Find technical vulnerabilities and fix them on a timeline that matches the risk.

children.title: Configuration management
children.summary: Define secure configurations and notice when they drift.

children.title: Information deletion
children.summary: Delete information when there is no reason left to keep it.

children.title: Data masking
children.summary: Hide personal or sensitive data when the real values are not required.

children.title: Data leakage prevention
children.summary: Put measures in place so sensitive data is harder to send to the wrong place.

children.title: Information backup
children.summary: Back up information and prove you can restore it.

children.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
children.summary: Have enough redundancy for the availability you commit to.

children.title: Logging
children.summary: Log security-relevant activity and keep those logs usable.

children.title: Monitoring activities
children.summary: Watch systems for unusual activity and follow up.

children.title: Clock synchronization
children.summary: Keep system clocks aligned so logs and evidence share one timeline.

children.title: Use of privileged utility programs
children.summary: Restrict tools that can bypass normal security controls.

children.title: Installation of software on operational systems
children.summary: Control what software can be installed on production systems.

children.title: Networks security
children.summary: Protect the network, not only the individual servers.

children.title: Security of network services
children.summary: Know the security features you require from network services.

children.title: Segregation of networks
children.summary: Separate networks when a flat network would spread a failure or an attack.

children.title: Web filtering
children.summary: Reduce exposure to malicious or inappropriate sites from work devices.

children.title: Use of cryptography
children.summary: Use cryptography where it protects confidentiality or integrity, and manage the keys.

children.title: Secure development life cycle
children.summary: Build security into how software is designed, built, and released.

children.title: Application security requirements
children.summary: State the security requirements for an application before it is built.

children.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
children.summary: Follow engineering principles that keep systems understandable and defensible.

children.title: Secure coding
children.summary: Write code in a way that avoids the common classes of implementation flaws.

children.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
children.summary: Test security before a change is accepted into production.

children.title: Outsourced development
children.summary: Keep security oversight when someone else writes the code.

children.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
children.summary: Keep production separate from the places where people experiment.

children.title: Change management
children.summary: Approve and record changes to production systems.

children.title: Test information
children.summary: Protect real personal or customer data if it is ever used in a test.

children.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
children.summary: Plan audit tests so they don't take production down or expose data.
